title: Hybrid machine learning guides experimental discovery of multicomponent metallic glasses
summary: Hybrid classification and regression models with physically motivated descriptors, trained on about 5,000 metallic-glass compositions, guided exploration of multicomponent alloy compositions. Researchers synthesized 23 selected compositions: 12 predicted glass-formers produced glass in bulk, ribbon or both, while 11 predicted negative comparisons did not form glass under the tested preparation conditions. Six of the positive designs formed bulk glass; six formed glassy ribbons only. These selected experiments are not an unbiased estimate of global predictive accuracy. Some authors disclosed inventorship on a filed patent related to the new bulk compositions; composition-level prior art and independent replication remain open.
ai_technology: Hybrid classification/regression models including adaptive boosting, SVM, KNN and rational-quadratic Gaussian-process regression

source_review.scope: Primary publisher full indexed article and institutional full-text copy, methods, results, date, affiliation and patent disclosure.

evidence.tested: The study reports synthesis and diffraction/thermal characterization of selected predicted positive and negative compositions.
evidence.unknown: Selected validation set, not unbiased global accuracy; patent inventorship disclosed and composition-level novelty/replication remain open.
evidence.ai_role: Hybrid models trained on prior metallic-glass data prioritized compositions for synthesis and measurement.
